intro: Philadelphia listings advertise non-climate 10x10 units from about $63, while typical non-climate 10x10 street rates run about $136–$140/month. Rates are down slightly year over year, but the city has only about 3.5 square feet of storage per person, and once the move-in special ends and the first existing-customer increase lands, the six-month average still sits well above the banner price.

units.notes: Locker / closet size. Fixed fees dominate the true cost at this size. Climate-controlled street rate ~$62; climate promos from about $5.
Walk-in closet; studio overflow. No reliable lowest-promo figure published for this size (gap). Climate-controlled ~$100.

Most rented size. City average $136, down 1.5% YoY (StorageCafe, Sep 2026); StorageUnitCosts lists the same $136 for August 2026, down 2.9% YoY. Philadelphia metro averages $140, down 3.2% YoY (Storage Stats). Climate-controlled ~$149.
Two-bedroom contents. Estimate: single source (StorageCafe, Sep 2026). Climate-controlled ~$194.
Three-bedroom home or a car. Climate-controlled ~$244.

local_tips: Location drives price: StorageCafe lists Parkwood (~$91), Olney (~$95) and Allegheny West (~$107) among the cheapest areas for a standard unit, while Northeast Philadelphia Airport (~$384) and Logan Square (~$244) run highest.
Philadelphia rates tend to be lowest around December and highest in June (StorageCafe).

About 112,000 sq ft of new storage is due in Philadelphia in 2026, down about 46% from 2025 (StorageCafe). Supply is thin at 3.5 sq ft per capita, so a cheap promo in Center City is rarer than one in the Northeast.
Extra Space charges a $50 admin fee (per StorageUnitCosts), higher than our $29 default; adjust the calculator if your facility charges more.
